newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pay TV deal not critical to Australia float - Optus.
newsitem.headline: Pay TV deal not critical to Australia float - Optus.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd chief executive officer Ziggy Switkowski said on Tuesday that a restructure of the pay television industry was not critical to the telecommunications group's proposed float this year.
Investors have expected a deal between Australia's pay televsion players to stem the flood of losses, estimated at about A$1.5 billion, the industry has chalked up since 1993.
Optus' main rival in pay TV is Foxtel, jointly owned by Telstra Corp AOT.AX and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and satellite TV operator Australis Media Ltd.
Despite the need for some need for a pay TV industry restructure, Optus Vision's pay-TV business was in good shape, Switkowski said.
"The economics of the pay TV arm Optus Vision is pretty strong," Switkowski said.
Switkowski said nine percent of Australian households were pay TV subscribers and Optus Vision has 185,000 subscribers.

He said Optus has been in talks with Telstra since Christmas about sharing their respective pay TV infrastructure. The two group's are spending a total of about A$7.0 billion on broadband cable networks, which would also carry telephony services.
But, he added Optus had not discussed the pay TV issue with Rupert Murdoch on his recent visit to Australia.
Australia's other major media player Kerry Packer has an interest in Australis through his family controlled media group Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL)
